decision: Every channel publishes one canonical order contract to an event bus; partners get adapters
why: Point-to-point integrations multiply with every new channel and partner.
alternative: Each channel calls each carrier and the tax gateway directly.
value: Adding a carrier is one adapter, not N integrations.

decision: Sampled events travel as packets; edge color is health
why: Operators need to see where flow slows down, not just a red number.
alternative: A table of partner metrics only.
value: A degraded edge is visible from across the room.

decision: The log tail streams over a Broadcast channel shared by every open console
why: During an incident several people watch the same stream and must see the same lines.
alternative: Each console polls a logs API.
value: One stream, many viewers, no extra load on the log store.

decision: AI triage links the DLQ spike to the partner changelog and proposes a mapping
why: The slowest part of an integration incident is finding what changed on the partner side.
alternative: Alert with the raw error and let on-call search.
value: Diagnosis in one card; a person still approves the mapping and the replay.

decision: Each adapter owns its circuit breaker and reports its state
why: One slow partner must not exhaust shared threads or stall the bus.
alternative: Global retries with a shared timeout.
value: Failures stay bounded to the partner that has them.
